analysis.title: Prime Services Weekly Report, October 23, 2026 (Friday 10/16 – Thursday 10/22)
key_insights: The GS Equity Fundamental L/S Performance Estimate fell -1.28% between 10/16 and 10/22 versus MSCI World TR -0.76%, driven by beta of -0.98% and alpha of -0.30% on short side losses.
The GS Equity Systematic L/S Performance Estimate fell -1.26% over the same period, driven by alpha of -1.63% on short side losses, partly offset by beta of +0.38%.

Overall book gross leverage rose 0.6 pts to 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 0.9 pts to 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year). The overall L/S ratio fell 0.7% to 1.597 (3rd percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 0.8 pts to 211.7% (63rd percentile 1-year). Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 1.7 pts to 47.0%, a 1-year low.
Beta-adjusted fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 1.9 pts to 226.5% (25th percentile 1-year). Beta-adjusted net leverage fell 3.5 pts to 60.4%, a 1-year low.
Global equities were net sold for a third straight week (-0.6 SDs 1-year). De-grossing accelerated, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4 to 1.
Regional flows were split. North America and EM Asia were net sold, while DM Asia and Europe were net bought.
Single stocks were net sold for a sixth straight week, driven by long sales. Macro products were net bought for the first time in 3 weeks, driven by long buys.
7 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led in dollar terms by TMT sectors (Info Tech plus Comm Svcs) and Energy. Staples, Real Estate and Cons Disc were the most net bought.

HFs net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months, with short and long sales at 1.4 to 1. North America (short and long sales) and Europe (long sales) were net sold, while Asia saw little net activity.
Within Energy, selling in Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels outpaced modest buying in Energy Equipment & Services.

The Prime book is over-weight Energy versus MSCI World by +0.5% (89th percentile 1-year, 69th percentile 5-year). Gross/Net Energy allocation is 4.9%/4.8% (90th/95th percentile 1-year, 39th/55th percentile 5-year).

Staples was the most dollar net bought global sector as HFs bought at the fastest pace in 10 weeks, driven by long buys and short covers (1.4 to 1). North America led, with Europe buying through short covers.
Within Staples, buying was led by Staples Distribution & Retail, Personal Care Products and Household Products.
The Prime book is under-weight Staples versus MSCI World by -3.7% (38th percentile 1-year, 64th percentile 5-year). Gross/Net Staples allocation is 4.6%/1.4%.

The largest regional flow changes were in Europe, with long sales of -1.72 SDs and short covers of +1.37 SDs. The largest sector flow changes were Health Care long sales (-1.57 SDs) and Comm Svcs short sales (-2.01 SDs).

sector_views.rationale: HFs net sold at the fastest pace in over 5 months, but the Prime book remains over-weight versus MSCI World by +0.5% (89th percentile 1-year).
Net buying was the fastest in 10 weeks, but the Prime book is still under-weight versus MSCI World by -3.7%.
TMT sectors led net selling in dollar terms. The Prime book is under-weight Info Tech versus MSCI World.
The Prime book is over-weight, with long sales of -1.57 SDs the largest sector flow change.

risk_factors: Short side losses drove both fundamental and systematic L/S underperformance for the week.
De-grossing is accelerating, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4 to 1.
Net leverage is at or near 1-year lows across the book, which signals reduced directional exposure.
vol_and_positioning: Overall book gross leverage is 312.3% (79th percentile 1-year, 93rd 3-year, 96th 5-year). Net leverage is 71.8% (3rd percentile 1-year). T12M net high is 82.9%.
Fundamental L/S net leverage is 47.0%, a 1-year low (0th percentile 1-year, T12M average 55.7%). Beta-adjusted net is 60.4%, also a 1-year low.
The overall L/S ratio is 1.60 (3rd percentile 1-year, T12M high 1.80, average 1.69).
De-grossing continued, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4 to 1 as global equities were net sold for a third straight week.
Single stocks were net sold for a sixth straight week, while macro products (index and ETF) were net bought for the first time in 3 weeks.
The market table lists VIX at 19.03 (+15.6% WoW) and SPX realized correlation at 9.8% (-1.5 pp WoW).
